findings.text: Both power headers use a conventional include guard macro that marks the header as already seen to prevent repeated inclusion.
System power events use negative one for the invalid marker and zero for the on condition, with remaining base conditions each assigned a distinct single bit from bit zero through bit eleven.
Composite sleep and directed suspend resume values combine a direction marker with a user remote auto or second direction marker rather than introducing new bit positions.
Ready made messages exist for each major power condition and each directed suspend resume combination, each carrying the event value that shares its name.

An auto test reports true when the auto marker is present in a message event, a no wakeup test reports true when freeze or quiesce is present, and a prethaw name is defined as another name for the quiesce value.

Runtime power status moves among active resuming suspended suspending and blocked conditions with a separate invalid marker, where active is the zero baseline and the other conditions follow as successive enumerated steps after an explicit negative invalid value.
Runtime requests enumerate none idle suspend autosuspend and resume in that order starting from zero for none, expressing the pending work that the runtime framework should perform.

Subsystem power data pairs a spin lock with a reference count and optionally carries clock power state including a sleep capability marker plus a mutex and a list together with an optional generic domain linkage when the corresponding build options are enabled.

The spin lock inside subsystem power data guards its reference count and associated list state, while the optional clock mutex serializes clock operations that may sleep separately from the spin protected fast path.

Device power management driver flags assign four independent single bit positions starting at bit zero to control direct complete prohibition, smart prepare, smart suspend, and permission to skip resume.

Per device power information records the current power message, wakeup and async choices, core owned list and preparation markers, a driver flags word, a spin lock, an optional subsystem link, an optional quality of service link, a latency tolerance callback, and a driver core owned detach marker.

When system sleep is configured the per device record adds list and synchronization plus wakeup linkage and a set of one bit markers for core ownership and wake behavior, while the minimal build keeps only a single wake intent marker.
When runtime management is configured the per device record adds timer and work and wait facilities plus usage accounting and request and status state with error and delay and time accumulators.

The spin lock inside per device power information serializes updates to its flags counters timers and status fields, with several markers documented as owned exclusively by the power core, some set by subsystems or the driver core, and the subsystem link owned by the subsystem.

A power domain descriptor groups standard power callbacks together with lifecycle hooks for starting, detaching with a power off choice, activating, synchronizing and dismissing a device, plus a hook to select a performance state.
When reporting is enabled a suspend result helper forwards the calling function name together with device operation name and status to a core reporting routine inside a single execution guard.

When system power management is unavailable the global device power lock operations do nothing, suspend start reports success without action, result reporting is discarded, waiting for another device reports success, iteration over devices performs no callback, and all generic prepare suspend resume freeze thaw restore poweroff and complete hooks are null.
Device ordering for power transitions enumerates four cases meaning no constraint, device after parent, parent before device, and device last.
Operating performance change notifications distinguish addition, removal, enabling, disabling, and voltage adjustment as successive enumerated values starting at zero.

An operating point supply record carries nominal voltage with minimum and maximum bounds plus current and power measures, a dynamic entry record carries turbo marking with level frequency and voltage, and a lookup key carries frequency level and bandwidth.

An operating point configuration record optionally names clocks with a clock setup callback, names a property, provides a regulator setup callback, lists supported hardware versions with a count, names regulators, and identifies a required device with an index, with an unset level defined as the maximum unsigned thirty two bit value.

When operating point support is disabled, table acquisition helpers report operation not supported or return the input unchanged on reference acquisition and do nothing on release, while bandwidth voltage power frequency and level accessors return zero and supply retrieval reports operation not supported.

When disabled, exact floor and ceiling searches by frequency with or without an index, searches by level and by bandwidth, key based lookup, required state reading, turbo testing, count and latency and suspend frequency queries, and point translation return operation not supported or zero or false, while reference acquisition returns its input and release does nothing.

When disabled, dynamic addition reports operation not supported while removal helpers do nothing, voltage adjustment and enable and disable report success without action, notifier and configuration and clock setup and translation and rate and point selection and sharing setup report operation not supported except sharing query which reports invalid argument, and table removal and regulator synchronization follow the same disabled pattern.

When disabled, frequency table initialization reports invalid argument and release does nothing, device tree and mask based table addition report operation not supported while removals and one unregistration path do nothing, sharing and descriptor and node lookups return operation not supported or null or false, energy registration reports operation not supported, and power and required state and interconnect queries report operation not supported, except one unregistration variant that delegates to the energy model.

Small convenience helpers build a one entry data record or a configuration record holding only regulators, supported versions, clock names, regulator callback or property name and then delegate to the generic dynamic addition or configuration entry points, with matching release helpers delegating to a single clear operation, while the plain frequency accessor delegates to the indexed variant with index zero and the level setter finds the exact level and then applies the found point.
